title: Stable Frobenius affine charts and their equalizer presentations
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and let $X_0$ be a finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Set $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ [def-pc-fibre-product], let $m\geq1$, put $Q=q^m$, and let $h=\Phi^m$ for the $k$-linear scheme Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Write $F$ for the equalizer of $h$ and $1_X$, namely the fibre product $X\times_{X\times_kX,(1,h),\Delta_X}X$, where $\Delta_X=(1,1)$. There is a finite affine open cover $U_{0,j}=\operatorname{Spec}A_{0,j}$ of $X_0$ with each $A_{0,j}$ a finitely generated $k_0$-algebra. Every affine open $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0\subseteq X_0$ is preserved by the $Q$-power Frobenius on $X_0$, and $U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$ is preserved by $h$. For $B=A_0\otimes_{k_0}k$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(a\otimes c)(a'\otimes c')=aa'\otimes cc'$ and unit $1\otimes1$, the induced $k$-algebra endomorphism is $\phi(a\otimes c)=a^Q\otimes c$. With $J=(\phi(b)-b:b\in B)$, the first projection induces a canonical isomorphism $F\times_XU\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ over $U$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every presentation $A_0=k_0[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/\mathfrak a$ (polynomial rings as in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]), the canonical identification $B\simeq k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/\mathfrak a_k$ sends $J$ to the ideal generated by the classes of $t_i^Q-t_i$, where $\mathfrak a_k$ is the ideal generated by the coefficientwise images of $\mathfrak a$. Thus the equalizer chart has coordinate algebra $k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(\mathfrak a_k,t_1^Q-t_1,\ldots,t_r^Q-t_r)$, with the quotient map from $B$ as its inclusion on spectra. The equalizer identification agrees with restriction to any smaller model affine open. No separatedness of $X_0$ is assumed. Here an ideal of a ring $R$ is an additive subgroup stable under multiplication by elements of $R$; $(S)$ denotes the ideal of finite sums of ring multiples of elements of $S$, and $R/L$ is the quotient by $u\sim v\iff u-v\in L$.

proof.text: Apply the definition of finite type to the affine base $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$: its inverse image $X_0$ has a finite affine open cover $U_{0,j}=\operatorname{Spec}A_{0,j}$ by finitely generated $k_0$-algebras. This is precisely the finite-cover equivalence in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. No separatedness enters.

source.place: Tag 01T1, definition-finite-type; finite-cover formulation in def-weil-finite-type-morphism

proof.text: The absolute $q$-power Frobenius has identity underlying map and acts on sections by $a\mapsto a^q$ [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. Its $m$-fold iterate therefore preserves every model open and acts by $a\mapsto a^{q^m}$. For any affine $U_0$, its inverse image $U$ in $X$ is $\operatorname{Spec}B$, $B=A_0\otimes_{k_0}k$, with its projections as in [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. By the defining base-change construction of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], $h$ preserves $U$; induction on $m$ in its affine formula gives $\phi(a\otimes c)=a^Q\otimes c$. The tensor algebra multiplication and unit are those of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property].

source.place: Tag 03SM, definition-absolute-frobenius; blueprint Step 0 and def-trf-scheme-frobenius affine formula

proof.text: Write $P_0=k_0[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$, $P=k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$, $D=P/\mathfrak a_k$, and $x_i=[t_i]\in A_0$. Coefficient extension followed by the quotient kills $\mathfrak a$, hence defines $\alpha:A_0\to D$, $[f]\mapsto[f_k]$: if representatives differ by an element of $\mathfrak a$, their images differ by an element of $\mathfrak a_k$. The tensor universal property gives $\theta:B\to D$, $a\otimes c\mapsto\alpha(a)c$. Conversely evaluate $P$ at $x_i\otimes1$ in $B$, using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For $f\in\mathfrak a$, its evaluation is $[f]\otimes1=0$; therefore this evaluation kills $\mathfrak a_k$ and defines $\eta:D\to B$. Both maps are $k$-algebra maps. The composite $\theta\eta$ fixes each $[t_i]$ and every scalar, so it fixes every polynomial class. The composite $\eta\theta$ sends $[f]\otimes c$ to $[f]\otimes c$ by evaluation and coefficient expansion; every element of $B$ is a finite sum of pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Thus both composites are identities. This constructs the specified canonical identification, without any flatness assertion.

Let $\pi:B\to B/J$. For every scheme $T$, the natural affine adjunction [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] identifies maps $T\to\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ with ring maps $v:B/J\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. Such maps are in bijection with ring maps $u:B\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ killing $J$: the inverse is $[b]\mapsto u(b)$, well defined because $u$ kills differences in $J$. Killing $J$ is equivalent to $u\phi=u$. By naturality of the same adjunction this says exactly that the associated $t:T\to U$ satisfies $h|_U\circ t=t$. On the other hand the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies maps $T\to F\times_XU$ with these same maps $t$: a map to $F$ is a pair $z,w:T\to X$ with $(z,hz)=(w,w)$, so $w=z$ and $hz=z$; requiring its first projection to lie in $U$ gives $z=it$. Since the open inclusion $i:U\to X$ is injective on maps (an open subscheme has the restricted sheaf), $hit=it$ is equivalent to $h|_U t=t$. The quotient projection gives the comparison $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)\to F\times_XU$; its maps out of every $T$ are bijective, so [lem-coef-joyal-homset-iso-detection] makes it an isomorphism. Its composite to $U$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\pi$.

source.place: Tag 01I1, lemma-morphism-into-affine; blueprint Step 0, equalizer quotient via its universal property

proof.text: Under Step 3 identify $B$ with $D$, and write $z_i=[t_i]$. Set $I=(z_i^Q-z_i)_i$. Every generator of $I$ is $\phi(z_i)-z_i$, so $I\subseteq J$. Conversely the two $k$-algebra maps $B\to B/I$ given by $\rho\phi$ and $\rho$ agree on each $z_i$ and on $k$ (the latter because $\phi$ is $k$-linear, not the absolute Frobenius on $B$). Composing with $P\to B$, the polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] makes them equal. Hence $\phi(b)-b\in I$ for every $b$, giving $J\subseteq I$. This also writes out the blueprint calculation: $u^n-v^n=(u-v)\sum_{s=0}^{n-1}u^{n-1-s}v^s$, and telescoping a product replaces one factor at a time, so each monomial difference $z^{Q\nu}-z^\nu$ is in $I$. Thus expanding $b$ as a polynomial over $k$ gives the same inclusion directly; no claim $c^Q=c$ for $c\in k$ is used.

The composite $P\to B\to B/J$ has kernel $(\mathfrak a_k,t_1^Q-t_1,\ldots,t_r^Q-t_r)$. Indeed a polynomial maps into the ideal of the classes $z_i^Q-z_i$ precisely when its class is a finite sum of their multiples; lifting these finitely many multipliers to $P$ leaves an element of $\mathfrak a_k$. The reverse containment follows by applying the quotient map. Explicitly $[f]\mapsto[[f]]$ gives an isomorphism from the displayed quotient of $P$ to $B/J$, with inverse $[[f]]\mapsto[f]$; changing a representative in either quotient changes the result by the displayed kernel. Step 4 then gives the asserted spectrum and identifies its map to $U$ with the quotient map from $B$, by contravariant functoriality of [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

For a smaller model affine $V_0\subseteq U_0$, Step 2 makes its base change $V$ stable too. Both $(F\times_XU)\times_UV$ and $F\times_XV$ represent maps $t:T\to V$ with $ht=t$, by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Their canonical identification sends each such $t$ to itself. The isomorphism constructed in Step 4 is characterized by exactly the same property and its map to $U$; after restriction it therefore agrees with the construction on $V$. This proves compatibility for arbitrary smaller affine opens, without assuming they are principal and without assuming affine intersections. Every argument is local on a stable model affine or uses a universal property, so no separatedness hypothesis is needed.
